Definition: from G575 and G991; to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard:--have respect.
BiblicalUsage: Once, about Moses. He esteemed the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt, for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward — he looked away from everything Egypt offered and fixed his eyes on what God promised.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse, and the whole of faith is in it: looking away from what is near to look intently at what is coming.
